pages.title: One cleaning contract for six offices saves GBP 56,000 a year
pages.notes: Open with the saving and the scope: one contract, six offices, GBP 56,000 a year.
pages.subtitle: Proposal to Example Freight Ltd

pages.title: One contract for six offices saves GBP 56,000 a year and is audited monthly
pages.notes: Give the proposal in three sentences: what changes, what it saves, and how it is checked every month.

blocks.lead: Three suppliers clean six offices for GBP 412,000 a year.
points: No two contracts end in the same month
The suppliers' own audits passed 82% of checks in 2026

blocks.lead: One contract saves most and takes the least effort to reach.
points: Renegotiating each contract saves about GBP 15,000 a year
An own cleaning team saves GBP 22,000 and takes a year to build

blocks.lead: GBP 356,000 a year, fixed for two years, with a monthly audit.
points: All six offices move to the new contract by March 2027
A decision by 4 December keeps the January start

pages.title: This proposal answers three questions
pages.notes: Name the three questions the proposal answers and move on.

items.name: Today
items.text: What does cleaning cost, and what goes wrong?

items.name: Options
items.text: Which ways are there to change it?

items.name: Offer
items.text: What do we offer, at what price, and from when?

pages.title: Riverside costs almost twice as much to clean as the smallest office
pages.notes: Start with the gap between the two ends of the chart. The difference is the reason for one contract.
pages.takeaway: Three suppliers clean six offices today, each to its own schedule.
points: The six offices cost GBP 412,000 a year together
No two contracts end in the same month
pages.alt: Bar chart of the yearly cleaning cost of six offices in GBP thousand, from 96 at Riverside down to 50 at Parkside, 412 in all.
pages.source: Source: Example Freight Ltd, supplier invoices 2026

pages.title: Three suppliers cost each office manager a day every month
pages.notes: Let the quote stand for a moment. It is the cost nobody sees in the invoices: a day a month for every office manager.
pages.quote: “I lose a day every month chasing three suppliers about cleans that were missed.”
pages.name: Jordan Example
pages.role: Office manager, Riverside, Example Freight Ltd
pages.source: Source: site walk at Riverside, 3 November 2026

pages.title: One contract saves most, and it is the first to be ready
pages.notes: Walk the options in the order shown. One contract saves most and is ready first; say that plainly.
pages.source: Source: Example Freight Ltd, supplier invoices 2026; Example Facilities Ltd, estimates of November 2026

pages.title: One contract is the only option that saves much for little effort
pages.notes: Read the matrix from the top left corner: much saved for little effort. Only one option sits there.
pages.takeaway: Only one option is both a large saving and a small change.
points: Renegotiating keeps three suppliers and three ways of auditing
An own team saves less and takes a year to build
pages.source: Source: Example Facilities Ltd, estimates of November 2026

pages.title: The offer comes down to three figures the offices can hold us to
pages.notes: These are the three figures the offices can hold us to. Say each once, with its unit.

figures.label: Saving
figures.note: GBP 412,000 today against GBP 356,000 offered, a cut of 14%.

figures.label: Audit pass rate
figures.note: Up from 82% in 2026; the fee falls by 2% in any quarter under it.

figures.label: Fixed price
figures.note: One contract with one end date, 31 December 2028.

pages.takeaway: The price is fixed for two years and tied to the audit result.
pages.source: Source: Example Facilities Ltd, offer of 12 November 2026

pages.title: All six offices cost GBP 356,000 a year under the offer, GBP 56,000 less
pages.notes: Do not read the table out. Give the total and the saving, and offer the office lines for questions.
pages.head: Cleaning cost by office, GBP thousand a year
pages.takeaway: Every office costs less; none pays for another's saving.
points: The price holds for two years from January 2027
pages.source: Source: Example Freight Ltd, supplier invoices 2026; Example Facilities Ltd, offer of 12 November 2026

pages.title: One page a month shows every office's checks and open actions
pages.notes: Show what the offices get every month: one page of checks and open actions. Point at one example on it.
pages.caption: Monthly audit report, sample page for February 2027
pages.alt: A one-page report with a table of six offices: checks made, checks passed, pass rate and open actions. 198 of 208 checks passed, 95%, with 10 actions open.
pages.takeaway: You see the same report our site lead does.
points: Shared on the fifth working day of each month
The fee falls by 2% in any quarter under 95%
pages.source: Source: Example Facilities Ltd, audit report template, November 2026

pages.title: All six offices move to the new contract by March 2027
pages.notes: Give the end date first, March 2027, then the first office to move.

steps.detail: Staff at all six offices are told the same week.
The two largest offices go first, with daily checks.
You see the same report our site lead does.
Each on the day its old contract ends.

pages.title: A decision by 4 December keeps the January start
pages.notes: Say what a decision by 4 December makes possible, and what slips if it comes later.

steps.action: Walk all six offices with our site lead
steps.detail: Half a day; we bring the audit checklist.

steps.action: Confirm the staff who wish to transfer
steps.detail: Their terms stay as they are.

pages.title: We ask for a decision by 4 December 2026
pages.notes: Repeat the ask and the date. Say whom to reach.
pages.small: Prices exclude VAT. The offer is valid until 31 January 2027.

pages.title: Appendix
pages.notes: Backup pages follow. Use them only if a question calls for them.

pages.title: The smaller offices cost most a square metre, today and under the offer
pages.notes: Backup for a question on cost a square metre: the smaller offices cost most, today and under the offer.
pages.head: Cleaning cost by floor area, 2026 and offered
pages.takeaway: The offer lowers the cost a square metre at every office by about a seventh.
points: Floor areas are from the 2026 office register
Costs are a year's cleaning divided by the floor area
pages.source: Source: Example Freight Ltd, office register and supplier invoices 2026; Example Facilities Ltd, offer of 12 November 2026

pages.title: The price covers daily cleaning, supplies and the monthly audit
pages.notes: Backup for a question on scope: what the price covers and what it does not.
pages.statement: One price covers what the six offices need in a normal month.

points.point: In the price: cleaning on every working day
points.detail: Desks, floors, meeting rooms and washrooms, to the schedule each office keeps today.

points.point: In the price: supplies and the monthly audit
points.detail: Soap, paper and cleaning products, and the report shared with you each month.

points.point: Quoted apart: outside windows and deep carpet cleans
points.detail: Twice a year at most offices; each job is quoted before it is booked.
